title: A Swedish copper coin from 1644 weighed 19.7 kg and measured 30 by 70 cm

cover.alt: A tall, rippled rectangular sheet of copper with a round stamp at each corner and one in the middle reading 8 daler.

body: Sweden was rich in copper, and for over a century it paid with **plate money** (*plåtmynt*): flat copper slabs stamped with their value. Each plate was minted at full weight, so the copper in it was worth as much as the silver coins of the same denomination. Copper is much cheaper than silver, so a high-value plate had to be enormous. The 10-daler plate dated 1644 weighs **19.7 kg** and measures 30 × 70 cm; Guinness World Records lists it as the heaviest coin ever made for circulation. Plates like these stayed common in Sweden until 1776.

slides.heading: Smallest and largest plate values
slides.note: Because each plate held its full value in copper, a bigger value meant a heavier plate.

left.label: Carry the plates
left.text: Haul slabs of copper, each 10-daler piece weighing almost 20 kg, to wherever you need to pay.

right.label: Carry a receipt
right.text: Leave the plates in a warehouse and hand over the paper receipt you were given for them.

slides.heading: Copper that became paper
slides.text: The plates were so heavy that they were often stored in warehouses. Depositors got receipts, and those receipts sometimes changed hands as money in their own right: one of the earliest instances of paper currency.

slides.prompt: About 25,500 of the 10-daler plates were minted between 1644 and 1655. How many survive today?
slides.answer: Just seven, says Guinness World Records
slides.detail: That is roughly one survivor for every 3,600 plates minted.

slides.question: Why did Sweden's plate coins have to be so large?
options: They held their full value in copper
To make them hard to steal
Sweden had no mint for small coins
slides.explanation: Each plate contained as much copper as its value in silver. Copper is far cheaper than silver, so a plate worth 10 daler needed almost 20 kg of it.

source.label: Guinness World Records: Heaviest coin for circulation
